notes: PSA 12 ng/mL. PI-RADS 3. PSAD 0.12. Prostate volume 103 mL. csPCa 0.46.

note_sections.t: Multidisciplinary team review for treatment planning following recent histological confirmation of intermediate-risk prostate adenocarcinoma.

Long-standing referral for management of newly diagnosed prostate cancer in a 66-year-old civil engineer. The patient reports a gradual rise in prostate-specific antigen over the past eighteen months, progressing from 2.2 ng/mL in late 2023 to 12.0 ng/mL currently, with a calculated velocity of 6.61 ng/mL per year. He manages hypertension and chronic kidney disease with valsartan, lisinopril, and metoprolol, with recent renal function showing a creatinine of 143 umol/L and eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73m². He is married, resides with his partner, and maintains a routine of daily twenty-minute walks while abstaining completely from alcohol. Recent non-urological appointments included an audiology assessment and an endocrine screening for thyroid function. He travels over ninety minutes to reach the clinic and prefers telephone follow-up, while his nephew serves as his designated next-of-kin.

Per rectum, the prostate gland feels symmetrically enlarged and smooth without palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with a clinical stage of cT1c. General examination reveals stable vital signs with a heart rate of 68 bpm and body mass index of 26.8 kg/m². The patient is in no acute distress, with clear lungs and regular cardiac rhythm on auscultation.

admin: Lives >90 min from clinic; phone follow-up preferred where clinically safe.
